title: Filter placeholders on date / datetime / time columns step around the temporal-comparand door and compare as text (wrong rows, no 400)
body:
repo:objectstack#5 · os-bill · session_01Utp6CbSphdunq2aJq7ktuY

Filing gate: out-of-scope finding from the `os-dev` of #34938 (PR #35391), class a, filed by seat 5 (area ux-1) on the seat's word. ⛔ Not a claim. Pre-existing class on main, not introduced by #35391.

## What happens

The temporal-comparand door refuses a non-temporal literal compared against a `date` / `datetime` / `time` column (`INVALID_FILTER`, 400). But `isUninterpretableTemporalComparand` in `packages/core` steps around every known placeholder as written (`classifyFilterToken !== null`), and after resolution `judgeResolvedToken` checks only date-macro kinds. So a context placeholder (and, once #35391 lands, a period-key placeholder) reaches the driver and is compared as text.

Measured with `engine.find` on SqlDriver (SQLite) and InMemoryDriver, both the same; not measured over HTTP:

- `{current_user_id}` on a `date` column: `$lt` returns every row, `$eq` / `$gte` return no rows, all 200.
- The same comparisons with the literal value: refused, `INVALID_FILTER` 400.
- `{current_week_start}` with `$gte`: correct (a date macro is judged).

A list view, dashboard widget or RLS-adjacent filter that names a non-date placeholder on a temporal column silently returns wrong rows instead of an authoring error.

## Expected

The step-around applies to date-macro placeholders only. Context and period-key placeholders on a temporal column are judged like the literal they resolve to (refused 400), or refused as written.

## Done when

Pins for `{current_user_id}` (and `{current_iso_week}` if #35391 has merged) on date, datetime and time columns answer 400 on both drivers, `{current_week_start}` still resolves, and the door's ablation turns the pins red.

Dedupe words: temporal comparand placeholder step-around, isUninterpretableTemporalComparand, judgeResolvedToken, context token date column, period-key.
